All-lowercase is accepted, all-uppercase is accepted, ANY mixed case is rejected -- including mixing between the HRP and the data part.

findings.rule: argparse layer: --a and --b are both required; missing either exits 2 with usage on stderr. Extra positionals / unknown options exit 2 ("unrecognized arguments"). A value that begins with '-' must be given with the `=` form — `--b -x` exits 2 ("expected one argument") while `--b=-x` is accepted as data. `-a`/`-b` short forms do not exist. Duplicate flags: LAST one wins. `-h` prints help to stdout and exits 0. Argument order is irrelevant.

findings.rule: Extremely large inputs are handled cleanly and fast: 1000, 5000, 20009, 50000 and 131065-character --a/--b values all return (None, None) rc 0 in well under a second, with no memory blowup or hang. Above ~131065 bytes the kernel refuses the exec (E2BIG) before the program ever runs — an OS limit (MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 131072), not a program behavior, so a Node port has no equivalent obligation.

findings.rule: Structural preconditions on --b that a port must reproduce: the last '1' must be at index >= 1 (so a leading '1' with nothing before it fails), and at least 6 characters must follow it. Every character after the last '1' must be in the Bech32 charset "qpzry9x8gf2tvdw0s3jn54khce6mua7l" — the excluded characters 1, b, i, o (and their uppercase forms) in the data part all fail.
